:::{.definition data-title="Boundary Points"}

For
[[knowledge-mathematics-analysis-functional-analysis-metric-spaces|metric space]]
$(X,d)$ a **boundary point** for subset $A\subseteq X$ is a point $x\in X$ such
that for all $\epsilon >0$:
1. $B_\epsilon(x)\cap A\neq\emptyset$
2. $B_\epsilon(x)\cap A^{c\neq}\emptyset$
The **set of all boundary points** is commonly denoted by
$$
\partial A:=\{x\in X:x\text{ is a boundary point for }A\}
$$

:::

Note the following obvious results follow from the definition:
1. If $A\subset X$ is an [[open-sets-closed-sets-on-metric-spaces|open set]]
   then $A\cap\partial A=\emptyset$.
2. If $A\subseteq X$ is a [[open-sets-closed-sets-on-metric-spaces|closed set]]
   then $A\cap\partial A=A$.
